ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the left side of the figure is the closed circuit in which coil A is located, and the right side of the coil is connected to a vertical straight wire a; the right side shows two parallel plates, the upper plate labeled P1 and the lower plate labeled P2, and plasma gas flow is injected from left to right between the two plates. In the external circuit on the right, there is a vertical straight wire b adjacent and parallel to a, and b connects the upper and lower parts of the external circuit on the right. The diagram also marks the magnetic field B inside coil A as vertically upward. Then reason: the vertically upward magnetic field B inside coil A increases uniformly with time. According to Lenz's law, the magnetic field produced by the induced current should be vertically downward to oppose the increase of the original magnetic flux. Combining the winding direction of the coil in the figure and judging with the right-hand screw rule, the direction of the induced current in straight wire a in the left circuit is from top to bottom. It is known that straight wires a and b attract each other; parallel straight wires attract when their currents are in the same direction, so the current in b should also be from top to bottom. In the external circuit on the right, the current in b is from top to bottom, indicating that the current in the external circuit flows out from the end of the upper plate P1, passes through the external circuit and b, and flows to the end of the lower plate P2. Therefore P1 is the positive plate, and P2 is the negative plate. The plasma moves from left to right. If P1 is positive and P2 is negative, then positive ions should deflect upward and negative ions downward. For a positive ion, the Lorentz force direction is q(v×B), where the velocity v is to the right. To make the force on the positive ion upward, the magnetic field B must be perpendicular to the paper inward.
